raw_response:
I am old now, and there are only two of us in the house, so I cannot spread myself too thin. I will keep most of the land in the wheat-maize rotation because that is the steady way here, and I will leave a smaller piece for cotton. Cotton can make some money, but it takes more hand work, especially picking, so I do not want too much of it. This year I will put about 7 mu into wheat then summer maize on the same ground, and 3.1 mu into cotton. I will farm the same way I know: not too fancy, not too risky, and I will keep some cash in hand because pumping water and buying fertilizer both cost money.

For wheat, I will follow the usual village timing, sow in early October and harvest in early June. I will not skimp too much on fertilizer because if wheat turns weak in spring, yield falls fast. I will put most fertilizer before sowing and one more time at jointing if the crop needs it. I have well water, so I will use it, but only a few times because electricity and pumping cost money. After wheat harvest, I will rush to plant maize right away on that same land. There is no time to do heavy tillage then, so I will keep it simple. For cotton, I will plant a smaller area in April. I will not push cotton too hard with fertilizer because I do not have much labor, and too much vegetative growth only gives me more trouble. If insects show up, I will spray, otherwise I will not waste money. This is not the biggest plan, but it is a steady one I can still manage with my own hands.
